hook.es: Todas las conexiones empiezan a ser imposibles de seguir.
hook.en: All the connections start to become impossible to follow.

objective: The growing complexity of the Parallel World forces the creation of Moon, a central command view. The Traveler sees the whole map for the first time — and how much is still dark/unexplored.

scenes.visuals: Wide shot: Peskids, the agent-creatures, the layered structure, all connected by countless glowing threads crossing and tangling
scenes.copy: Tenants. Workers. Agentes. Deployments. Costos. Todo empezó a ser imposible de seguir a simple vista.

scenes.visuals: A massive holographic globe rises at the center of a new control-room space, connected data nodes arranging themselves around it
scenes.copy: Necesitaban una torre de control. Nació Mission Control. Después, Opsly Moon.

scenes.description: The Traveler sees everything at once
scenes.visuals: The Traveler reaching toward the globe, NØVA beside him small in the frame, Peskids and other node-thumbnails visible around the globe's surface
scenes.copy: Desde ahí, The Traveler podía ver Peskids. Futuros tenants. Workers. Agentes. Máquinas. Salud del sistema. Costos.

scenes.visuals: The camera pulls back to reveal the globe is surrounded by many more dim, unlit regions than lit ones
scenes.copy: Pero mientras más control ganaba, más grande resultaba ser el mapa.

scenes.visuals: The Traveler standing quietly before the mostly-dark globe
scenes.copy: Aparecían mundos nuevos, todavía sin explorar. No menos. Más.

metadata.call_to_action: Ver todo el mapa, por primera vez.
metadata.thumbnail_concept: The Traveler standing before a floating map interface (Moon), most of it lit, large sections still dark

notes: Act VIII of the Origin Saga — see ../../canon/ORIGIN-SAGA.md.
Theme: the need for visibility/control once a system outgrows what one person can track by feel — Moon exists to see Peskids, future tenants, workers, agents, machines, health, and costs all at once.

Emotional conflict: awe at how far things have come, mixed with a paradox — the more control The Traveler gains, the bigger the map turns out to be. New unexplored worlds appear as he gains visibility, not fewer.
Visual motif: the map-with-dark-zones device, reused and paid off in Episode 13.
Real event / fictionalization boundary: see ../../canon/TIMELINE.md row 08.
Reference image: ../../../assets/reference/e08-mission-control-globe.jpg — near-literal match for Moon's holographic-globe interface.
